outcomes: A SQL migration body and the record that marks it applied can never disagree, because they commit or roll back together
Runtime migration status and drift inspection require only read access and never initialize or lock the state store
Re-applying a registered set is idempotent and any divergence between registry and store surfaces as drift before release
Rollback only ever runs SQL the author persisted, verified against its stored hash
nonGoals: Making all datasources one distributed atomic transaction
Inferring rollback SQL when a migration author did not provide it
Owning migration source registration or kind routing, which stay with go/migration-execution

requirements.text: Each migration body and its success state-store record commit in one transaction under the datasource advisory lock; failure rolls back that transaction and is never returned as applied.
Datasource targets execute in lexicographic order, SQL definitions execute in canonical name order, and rollback proceeds in reverse recorded execution order.
Already-applied matching migrations are skipped, stored hashes remain comparable to current definitions, and changed, missing, or pending definitions appear in the drift report.
Status and drift inspection never create the migration state store or acquire its writer lock; when the store does not exist yet, registered definitions are reported as pending.
Rollback runs only a persisted, hash-verified down body and refuses a missing or tampered reversal rather than guessing destructive SQL.
